canvas.purpose: The ground everything sits on: shell, reading column, panel inset fields.

panel.purpose: One step up: Outline rail, Tutor/Tailor panel, code blocks, palette trigger, Done chip.

raised.purpose: Two steps up: the open Lesson row, the active palette option, inline code, the primary button at rest.

over.purpose: Three steps up: the command palette body, the compact Approve button, primary button hover.

hair.purpose: The default divider and the global border colour. Divides regions; never wraps an object.

rule.purpose: The stronger divider: the note block's left rule, the table header rule, Approve hover.

fg.purpose: Lesson titles, open rows, strong emphasis, code keywords. 12.18-15.65:1 across all four surfaces.

fg-2.purpose: Body prose, unopened Lesson titles, Tutor answers. 7.58-9.75:1.

fg-3.purpose: Goal, counts, captions, quiet buttons, placeholders, code comments. 5.09-6.54:1.

fg-dim.purpose: Completion dates, minute estimates, keycaps, separators, palette group headers. 4.61-5.92:1.

mark.purpose: GRAPHICS ONLY, never text. 3.15-4.05:1. One consumer: the dashed rule for a Lesson not yet generated.

live.purpose: The one accent. The Lesson you are up to, plus the focus ring, caret and selection. 9.97:1 on graphite canvas; the paper twin #0a7f5f clears 4.98:1 on white and 3.95:1 on the topmost surface.

bad.purpose: One consumer: the hover state of the Tailor's Discard control. No red fill, badge or error surface ships.

select.purpose: Text selection. One of the browser surfaces the workspace still owns.

thumb.purpose: Thin scrollbar thumb, content-box clipped inside a 3px transparent border; #3a4048 on hover.

scroll-shade.purpose: Fades a horizontal scroller's edge while content sits past it; paired with a local cover layer so it disappears at the ends.

float.purpose: What leaves the document. --over on graphite, white on paper: a modal that steps down from its own page reads as a hole, not a layer. One consumer, the command palette.

scrim.purpose: The ground the command palette sits on. Heavier on paper than a naive inversion would give, because a white dialog on a white page needs the page pushed further back.

declaredUnspent.name: --live-dim
declaredUnspent.note: Declared in app/globals.css, in both grounds. Zero consumers in the components.

declaredUnspent.name: --live-wash
declaredUnspent.note: Declared in app/globals.css, in both grounds. Zero consumers in the components.

declaredUnspent.name: --warn
declaredUnspent.note: Declared in app/globals.css, in both grounds. Zero consumers in the components.

declaredUnspent.name: --radius
declaredUnspent.note: Declared but never read. The vendored Sidebar writes it to 0 on its header and content; nothing in this world reads it. The radius ramp is served by --radius-sm/md/lg.

display-lg.purpose: Persuade surfaces only: the landing's opening and closing statements. 3rem at 640px and up, 2.5rem below.

display-lg-sm.purpose: The same Persuade statement below 640px, at 2.5rem.

display.purpose: The Lesson title at 640px and up, capped at 22ch and text-balanced.

display-sm.purpose: The same Lesson title below 640px. The only responsive type step in the system.

title.purpose: The Course Topic at the head of the Outline rail; also the palette input.

body.purpose: Lesson prose and the Exercise task, at a 36rem measure that reads 64-75 characters per line.

body-sm.purpose: Note blocks, the Exercise check line, the Next-Lesson title.

ui-lg.purpose: Palette options and Tailor change summaries.

ui.purpose: The workhorse step: Outline rows, chrome, panel prose, code, tables, captions.

meta.purpose: The facts around the content: Lesson position, rail numbers, module counts.

label.purpose: The one uppercase tracked style. Module headings, Exercise, Goal, Next, table headers.

mono.purpose: Geist Mono. Code, result tables, inline code at 0.86em, keycaps at 0.6875rem.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: The only shadow in the system. The command palette, and nothing else. Offset and blur, never a halo. Two values: a shadow tuned for a dark ground reads as soot on a white one.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: Exponential ease-out. The shell never bounces. Every transition and animation uses it.

motion.name: dur-fast
motion.purpose: Row and colour transitions in the Outline rail.

motion.name: dur-slow
motion.purpose: Entrances: the palette opening (mk-open), the panel sliding in (mk-slide).

motion.name: mk-check
motion.purpose: The check strokes itself onto the Exercise just marked. Fires on a real mark only.

motion.name: mk-handoff
motion.purpose: The accent lifting into place on the next Lesson. The second half of the handoff.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Both end states remain, all movement drops.

breakpoints.name: sheet
breakpoints.note: At or below, both rails become sheets over a blurred scrim at min(22rem, 88vw); rail rows grow to 44px.

breakpoints.name: panel-costs-rail
breakpoints.note: At or below, opening the panel collapses the rail.

breakpoints.name: 2xl
breakpoints.note: A closed panel keeps its 21rem in reserve and the reading column centres in the region that leaves.

measurements.name: measure
measurements.note: 64-75 characters per line, measured across four real paragraphs.

measurements.name: reading-drift
measurements.note: Reading column drift when the rail or the panel toggles, at 1280, 1440, 1600 and 1920.

measurements.name: outline-density
measurements.note: All Lesson rows visible with no scrolling at 1440x900, at 0.22rem row padding.

measurements.name: rail-stub
measurements.note: Collapsed rail width; the region takes calc(rail - 2.75rem) of left pad to stay put.

measurements.name: panel-reserve
measurements.note: From 2xl up, a closed panel keeps its width as right pad, so the region around the sentence is the same size open or closed.

measurements.name: contrast-floor
measurements.note: Text audited in-browser against its computed ground, in both themes.

themes.mechanism: A `dark` class on <html>, set before first paint by an inline script in the root layout. localStorage `mk-theme` wins; with nothing stored, prefers-color-scheme decides. Tailwind's dark: variant is remapped to the class with @custom-variant.
themes.structure: :root carries the complete paper palette and the shadcn/sidebar aliases, which read the semantic tokens and so follow the switch for free. .dark redeclares only the tokens that move.
themes.colorScheme: color-scheme moves with the theme, so browser-drawn scrollbars and form controls follow.
themes.floors: Both grounds hit the same contrast floors: 5.08/4.63 (paper) and 5.09/4.61 (graphite) for the quiet text steps against the topmost surface, 3.18/3.15 for the graphics-only mark. Audited in-browser against the computed ground: zero text below its floor in either theme.
themes.switch: One chrome control with no React state. The class is the state, the icon swap is CSS, and the choice is stored under mk-theme.

narrative.overview:
The Course is a working shell, not a reading room. It refuses the course player's checklist-and-progress-bar and the paper metaphor at once: everything on screen is information, and the only colour is where you are. The learner opens one Course at a laptop, often with an editor beside it, and the surface is built for that posture — dense, quiet, and legible in a long session.

Depth comes from light, and light has two settings. Graphite runs four steps up from #0f1012; paper runs four steps down from #ffffff. The ground flips, the system does not: in both, the sidebars sit one step off the reading ground, the open row sits two, and what floats sits at the top of the stack. A stored choice decides which ground a learner gets, and with no stored choice the operating system does; the class is set on <html> before first paint, so the shell is never briefly the wrong colour. A graphite canvas with three luminance steps up carries every layer in the product; hairlines divide but never enclose, and nothing on screen is a card. Type does the structural work that borders would do elsewhere: one sans for every word, one mono for every number that is data, and a single small tracked label style for the few things that need naming rather than reading.

Colour is rationed to one job. #4fd1a5 on graphite, #0a7f5f on paper, marks the Lesson you are up to and nothing else. Which Lesson is open is carried by a raised ground, so position and progress never compete for the same signal. Everything the learner has already finished is neutral, and everything not yet generated stays in place at a lower ink instead of disappearing or greying into a dead button. This world explicitly replaced a serif, paper-and-brass direction that was rejected outright; that vocabulary is anti-reference, not heritage.
keyCharacteristics: Two grounds, one system: graphite and paper, four surface steps each, zero cards, one shadow.
One accent with exactly one meaning, spent on roughly one row per screen.
Density as the point: all twenty Lessons visible at once on a laptop.
Geist and Geist Mono only; no serif anywhere in the product.
Reading column pinned to a 36rem measure that never moves when chrome opens.
Command palette as primary navigation, not a power-user shortcut.
Both rails are the shadcn Sidebar, adapted rather than reinvented.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: #4fd1a5 means exactly one thing: the Lesson you are up to. Roughly one row per screen carries it. If a second element wants the accent, the answer is a luminance step, not a hue.

rules.name: The Light, Not Line Rule
rules.body: Surfaces separate by luminance. A hairline divides two regions; it never wraps one to make an object. If a thing needs a border on all four sides to read, it is drawn wrong.

rules.name: The Graphics-Only Floor Rule
rules.body: --mark clears 3:1 and not 4.5:1. It is legal for meaning-bearing marks and illegal for text. Every other ink step is legal everywhere.

rules.name: The Two Family Rule
rules.body: Geist sets every word and Geist Mono every number that is data. No third face, and no serif anywhere in this product — the serif world was tried and rejected.

rules.name: The Tabular Data Rule
rules.body: Any number a learner might compare down a column — completion counts, Lesson numbers, dates, minute estimates, table cells, keycaps — carries .tnum (font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums lining). Prose numbers do not.

rules.name: The One Label Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one uppercase tracked style in the system, at 0.6875rem/600/0.06em. Uppercase is never used at any other size, and a label never grows into a heading.

rules.name: The One Right Edge Rule
rules.body: Every painted edge in the Lesson column — paragraph, code block, table, note, Exercise rule, footer rule — lands on the same right edge at 36rem. Code and tables scroll inside that edge; nothing reaches past it.

rules.name: The Fixed Sentence Rule
rules.body: Opening or closing chrome must not move the reading column. Zero drift is the acceptance test, not "close enough".

rules.name: The Whole Outline Rule
rules.body: Every Lesson in the Course is visible in the rail at once at 1440x900. Density is the feature; if a row wants more, it belongs on the Lesson, not in the rail.

rules.name: The Flat Shell Rule
rules.body: One shadow exists in this system and it belongs to the layer that leaves the document — a modal dialog. Everything else earns its depth from light.

rules.name: The No Card Rule
rules.body: Nothing in this product is a card. Not a Lesson, not a Tailor change, not a note, not a code block. Repeated content is a hairline-divided row list on its own ground; a note is a left rule; a code block is a luminance step. A stack of identically shaped boxes with a border and a radius is the failure mode this world was built against.

rules.name: The Stays In Place Rule
rules.body: A Lesson that has not been generated is drawn, ruled and inert. It is never hidden, never faded out, and never a disabled button — it holds its position in the Outline so the shape of the Course stays true.

rules.name: The Two Signals Rule
rules.body: Where you are up to is colour; what you have open is light. The two never swap and never combine on one row.

rules.name: The Both Grounds Rule
rules.body: A colour is a role with two values, not a value. Anything added to :root is answered in .dark unless it genuinely does not move, and a token is never hardcoded at a call site — a literal hex in a component is a colour that cannot follow the theme.

rules.name: The Constant Region Rule
rules.body: The reading column does not hold still by being nailed to the left; it holds still because the region around it never changes size. Anything that opens at an edge either reserves its width in advance or is not allowed to move the sentence.

dos: Do separate surfaces with luminance — canvas -> panel -> raised -> over — and use hairlines only to divide.
Do spend the accent on exactly one thing: the Lesson the learner is up to.
Do carry the open state with a raised ground and aria-current, never with colour.
Do hold body copy to the 36rem measure and land every painted edge in the reading column on it.
Do set every number that is data in Geist Mono or with .tnum, so columns of counts, dates and estimates line up.
Do keep unavailable entries in place, ruled at --mark and inert, with no hover and no click target.
Do give a scrolling code block or table its own edge fade rather than letting it bleed past the measure.
Do keep the full Outline visible at 1440x900; new row information goes on the Lesson instead.
Do move focus into a full-screen overlay, close it on Escape, mark the layers behind inert, and return focus to the control that opened it.
Do keep both end states and drop the movement under prefers-reduced-motion.
Do answer every new :root colour in .dark, and check both grounds against the contrast floors before shipping either.
Do reach for the vendored Sidebar for anything rail-shaped, and record an adaptation in the file at the line it changes.
Do mark a layer parked off the canvas inert, so it leaves the tab order with the pixels.
donts: Don't build cards. No bordered, radiused, shadowed boxes as page structure — the Tailor's change list included.
Don't introduce a second accent, a coloured status pill, a progress ring, a percentage, a streak, or an XP counter.
Don't spend the accent on done, on hover, on a button, on code syntax, or on anything but the live Lesson.
Don't set any part of this product in a serif, or reintroduce paper, vellum, ink stamps, folds, brass or a book metaphor. That world was tried and rejected outright.
Don't use --mark for text; it clears 3:1, not 4.5:1.
Don't render an unavailable Lesson as a disabled button, and don't list it in the command palette.
Don't add a shadow to anything that is not a floating modal layer; step the luminance instead.
Don't let opening or closing the rail or the panel shift the reading column by a single pixel.
Don't duplicate a control the panel already owns; while the panel is open, the shell shows no second control naming the same thing.
Don't add a radius outside 4/6/10px, or an uppercase style outside the one 0.6875rem label.
Don't hardcode a colour at a call site, or define one in only one ground.
Don't let the accent change meaning between the two grounds — it is darkened for paper, not repurposed.
Don't carry the theme in React state; the class on <html> is the state, and a mounted flag is a hydration seam waiting to show.
